name: Permissions API
plain: Lets a page ask what each permission is currently set to without prompting.
meaning: navigator.permissions.query() returns granted, denied or prompt for most permissions. It reveals which permissions you have granted or blocked, and a change event lets pages react live.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt; read only. States: granted, denied, prompt. A permissions policy block reports denied.

limits.headline: Can check whether you allowed or blocked a feature, without asking you
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page checks a setting
can: See if a permission is allowed, blocked, or still to be asked
Skip a pop up if you already said no
Update the page if you change a setting
Learn which sensors you have allowed on that site
cannot: See your choices for other sites
Turn a feature on without your yes
See states for every feature; some names are not supported

story.what_it_is: Lets a page check whether you already allowed, blocked or never answered a permission, without asking.

marketing.name: Permissions API
marketing.pitch: Docs describe it as a way for pages to check permission status before asking.

story.for_you: You never see it. The page just looks at your earlier answers and decides whether to show a pop-up or a helpful button. It can also see when you change your answer later.
story.for_makers: Asking for a permission at the wrong time annoys people and gets denied for good. The API lets sites ask only when it makes sense, and show a help message when the answer is blocked. It also reveals your settings, which can be used in a fingerprint.

use_cases.example: A video call page checks if the camera is already allowed and skips straight to the call, or shows a how-to-unblock note.
A maps site only shows the Use my location button if location is not blocked.
A browser game asks for microphone access only if it has not been blocked, and shows tips otherwise.
A news site waits to ask about notifications until it knows you have not blocked them.
A fraud tool reads the pattern of allowed and blocked permissions as part of a device profile.
A web app shows a status panel that lists which features are allowed.
A store locator checks location permission before showing a nearby stores prompt.

technical_bounds: Firefox lacks several names such as clipboard-read
